decision: SELECT TypeScript closure ownership over the shared native Fetch admission path for a single-session fresh revocable display source.
constraints: Node and browser ESM consumers need a fresh read/disconnect boundary compatible with the P12 lifecycle host; callback snapshots cannot establish freshness.
One active session per source, no queued starts, no credential persistence, no direct admission API and no extra display timer.
Reuse the versioned bounded decoder/session/schema path and frozen observation lease; no peer server changes or application authorization claims.

alternatives.assessment: Selected: private per-run Observation plus an explicit busy gate shares the already executable wire boundary. Native abort state and fresh view reads fit the existing synchronous host interface without a second queue, scheduler or parser. Static exported source types preserve consumer checks.

Can express the identical runtime ownership. No stronger cancellation behavior follows from removing TypeScript; typed declarations or checked annotations remain needed for consumer integration. No runtime performance difference is claimed.

The tagged Subscription implementation supports grouped teardown and closed-state ownership. This API requires one owner and explicit fresh pull reads, not subscriber fan-out or replay. A reactive graph still needs the same admission, expiry and restart rules; its additional ownership model does not materially improve this boundary.

Official documentation supports JavaScript runtimes, module interoperation and shared JVM/mobile logic. A shared client business layer could justify this later, but no present JVM deployment or common implementation contract exists. Host Fetch and explicit cancellation remain necessary; no material interoperability win is demonstrated.

Typed external bindings can model host functions and provide a credible compile-to-JavaScript client. They still require the same native async/session ownership and emitted JavaScript module boundary. No source-sharing or representation requirement establishes an advantage over the direct typed host API here.

limits: No cross-language runtime benchmark was executed; selection follows deployment interoperability and explicit one-session resource ownership.

Disconnect masks subsequent reads synchronously, but cannot erase previously copied views or guarantee remote deletion. Host Fetch must honor abort; otherwise the busy gate can remain held until settlement.
The containing product owns source authorization, initial start and any explicit restart after visibility/permission checks. No automatic authentication or reconnect.
Structural DOM and Node bundle tests are not actual browser accessibility, CORS, timing or installed-product acceptance.
No complete operator application, release-bound role-aware Help Center, physical actuation, targeting, tactical or security/availability qualification.
